The first season consisted of eight episodes which were released worldwide on Netflix on July 15, 2016,[[95]](#cite_note-97) in [Ultra HD](/wiki/Ultra-high-definition_television "Ultra-high-definition television") [4K](/wiki/4K_resolution "4K resolution"). The second season, consisting of nine episodes, was released on October 27, 2017, in HDR.[[96]](#cite_note-98)[[97]](#cite_note-99) The third season once again consists of eight episodes,[[98]](#cite_note-S3Directors-100) and was released on July 4, 2019.[[99]](#cite_note-S3Release-101) The fourth season, consisting of nine episodes, was released in two volumes on May 27 and July 1, 2022, respectively.[[100]](#cite_note-TheWrap-102) In February 2022, Netflix renewed the series for a fifth and final season.[[101]](#cite_note-103) The fifth season, consisting of eight episodes, premiered its first volume on November 26, 2025, the second on December 25, 2025, and the [series finale](/wiki/Series_finale "Series finale") on December 31.[[102]](#cite_note-Season5ThreeParts-104)

Shortly after the fourth season's release, viewers reported that Will's friends did not acknowledge his birthday in an episode of the season that took place on that day. The Duffers said in an interview that they could rectify the matter by changing its month, which they called "George Lucas-ing the situation", in reference to the [canon changes](/wiki/Changes_in_Star_Wars_re-releases "Changes in Star Wars re-releases") that [George Lucas](/wiki/George_Lucas "George Lucas") had made to the original *Star Wars* trilogy to match what the prequel trilogy had added.[[103]](#cite_note-variety_rework-105) Some viewers took this to imply that scenes from earlier seasons were also being edited, including one scene where Jonathan takes discreet pictures of a pool party that Steve, Nancy, and Barbara are holding. The writers stated that "no scenes from previous seasons have ever been cut or re-edited", including this scene.[[103]](#cite_note-variety_rework-105)

Thirty states have national parks, as do the [territories](/wiki/Territories_of_the_United_States "Territories of the United States") of [American Samoa](/wiki/American_Samoa "American Samoa") and the [U.S. Virgin Islands](/wiki/United_States_Virgin_Islands "United States Virgin Islands"). The state with the most national parks is [California](/wiki/California "California") with nine, followed by [Alaska](/wiki/Alaska "Alaska") with eight, [Utah](/wiki/Utah "Utah") with five, and [Colorado](/wiki/Colorado "Colorado") with four. The largest national park is [Wrangell–St. Elias](/wiki/Wrangell%E2%80%93St._Elias_National_Park_and_Preserve "Wrangell–St. Elias National Park and Preserve") in Alaska: at over 8 million acres (32,375 km2), it is larger than each of the [nine smallest states](/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_area "List of U.S. states and territories by area"). The next three largest parks are also in Alaska. The smallest park is [Gateway Arch National Park](/wiki/Gateway_Arch_National_Park "Gateway Arch National Park"), [Missouri](/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"), at 192.83 acres (0.7804 km2). The total area protected by national parks is approximately 52.4 million acres (212,000 km2), for an average of 833 thousand acres (3,370 km2) but a [median](/wiki/Median "Median") of only 220 thousand acres (890 km2).[[8]](#cite_note-acreage_report-8)

The national parks set a visitation record in 2024, with more than 94 million visitors;[[9]](#cite_note-:0-9) although overall visitation at the national parks in 2025 dropped by about 400,000.[[10]](#cite_note-:1-10) [Great Smoky Mountains National Park](/wiki/Great_Smoky_Mountains_National_Park "Great Smoky Mountains National Park") in North Carolina and Tennessee has been the most-visited park since 1944,[[11]](#cite_note-11) and had over 12 million visitors in 2024.[[9]](#cite_note-:0-9) In contrast, about 11,900 people visited the remote [Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve](/wiki/Gates_of_the_Arctic_National_Park_and_Preserve "Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve") in Alaska that same year.[[9]](#cite_note-:0-9)

Beryllium production saw a rapid increase during World War II due to the rising demand for hard beryllium-copper alloys and [phosphors](/wiki/Phosphor "Phosphor") for [fluorescent lights](/wiki/Fluorescent_light "Fluorescent light"). Most early fluorescent lamps used [zinc orthosilicate](/wiki/Zinc_orthosilicate "Zinc orthosilicate") with varying content of beryllium to emit greenish light. Small additions of magnesium [tungstate](/wiki/Tungstate "Tungstate") improved the blue part of the spectrum to yield an acceptable white light. Halophosphate-based phosphors replaced beryllium-based phosphors after beryllium was found to be toxic.[[92]](#cite_note-94)

Electrolysis of a mixture of [beryllium fluoride](/wiki/Beryllium_fluoride "Beryllium fluoride") and [sodium fluoride](/wiki/Sodium_fluoride "Sodium fluoride") was used to isolate beryllium during the 19th century. The metal's high melting point makes this process more energy-consuming than corresponding processes used for the [alkali metals](/wiki/Alkali_metals "Alkali metals"). Early in the 20th century, the production of beryllium by the thermal decomposition of [beryllium iodide](/wiki/Beryllium_iodide "Beryllium iodide") was investigated following the success of a similar process for the production of [zirconium](/wiki/Zirconium "Zirconium"), but this process proved to be uneconomical for volume production.[[93]](#cite_note-95)

Pure beryllium metal did not become readily available until 1957, even though it had been used as an alloying metal to harden and toughen copper much earlier.[[45]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEmsley200158-47) Beryllium could be produced by reducing beryllium compounds such as [beryllium chloride](/wiki/Beryllium_chloride "Beryllium chloride") with metallic potassium or sodium. The tsunami height that had been initially predicted by the [tsunami warning system](/wiki/Tsunami_warning_system "Tsunami warning system") was lower than the actual tsunami height; this error contributed to the delayed escape of some residents. The discrepancy arose as follows: in order to produce a quick prediction of a tsunami's height and thus to provide a timely warning, the initial earthquake and tsunami warning that was issued for the event was based on a calculation that requires only about three minutes. This calculation is, in turn, based on the maximum amplitude of the seismic wave. The amplitude of the seismic wave is measured using the [JMA magnitude scale](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%9E%E3%82%B0%E3%83%8B%E3%83%81%E3%83%A5%E3%83%BC%E3%83%89#気象庁マグニチュード_Mj "ja:マグニチュード"), which is similar to [Richter scale](/wiki/Richter_scale "Richter scale").
